description.en: France observes a range of public holidays shaped by revolutionary history, Christian traditions, and national remembrance. These holidays affect work schedules, school calendars, government services, and travel across the country. Most public holidays are observed nationwide, with businesses and public institutions typically closed or operating reduced hours.

sections.title: About France
sections.content: France, officially the French Republic, is a country primarily located in Western Europe. Its overseas regions and territories include French Guiana in South America, Saint Pierre and Miquelon in the North Atlantic, the French West Indies, and many islands in Oceania and the Indian Ocean. Metropolitan France shares borders with Belgium and Luxembourg to the north; Germany to the northeast; Switzerland to the east; Italy and Monaco to the southeast; Andorra and Spain to the south; and a maritime border with the United Kingdom to the northwest. Its metropolitan area extends from the Rhine to the Atlantic Ocean and from the Mediterranean Sea to the English Channel and the North Sea. Its 18 integral regions—five of which are overseas—span a combined area of 632,702 km2 (244,288 sq mi), with a total population estimated at over 69.1 million in 2026. Its capital, largest city and main cultural and economic centre is Paris.

sections.title: Important Notice
sections.content: Public holiday observance may vary by sector, region, or employer. Always confirm critical dates with official French government sources when planning travel, payroll, or business operations.

sections.title: How Public Holidays Are Observed in France
sections.content:
On most public holidays:

Government offices and schools are closed.
Banks are closed.
Many businesses close or operate reduced hours.
Public transport may run on holiday schedules.
Labour Day (May 1) is the most strictly observed closure nationwide.

sections.title: Why French Public Holidays Matter
sections.content:
Knowing Franceâ€™s public holidays helps with:

Business and payroll planning.
Travel and accommodation scheduling.
School calendar coordination.
Avoiding service disruptions.
Both residents and visitors benefit from understanding national closure patterns.

q.en: Are all public holidays observed nationwide in France?

a.en: While many holidays are national, some observances may be limited to specific regions, states, or territories.

q.en: Do businesses and stores close on public holidays in France?

a.en: Generally yes. Government offices, banks, and schools are closed. Essential services and some retail sectors may remain open or operate on reduced hours.

q.en: What happens if a public holiday falls on a weekend in France?

a.en: In many cases, if a national holiday falls on a Saturday or Sunday, the observance is moved to the following Monday, though this depends on specific local laws and the holiday in question.

q.en: Are public transport services affected by holidays in France?

a.en: Yes, public transportation often runs on a reduced Sunday or holiday schedule during national public holidays.

q.en: Are employees entitled to paid time off on public holidays in France?

a.en: Most full-time employees are legally entitled to a paid day off on national public holidays. Those who are required to work are typically eligible for premium pay or a substitute day off.
